governance.attested_by: miso18 seam-export-cap 2026-06-28 (KEEPER on faithfulness grounds, supersedes miso16 st-gas-intermediate)
governance.note: MISO's reference-price seam (build_reference_price_node) makes every neighbor's import bands AND export sinks available every hour. miso12 added a measured one-sided IMPORT deliverability cap (measured_seam_import_envelope) but the EXPORT direction stayed uncapped — so in the high-gas 2025 year (Henry Hub $3.52) the model ran cheap MISO coal hard and dumped the surplus out over the seam, flipping net interchange to net-EXPORT (model +17.97 vs actual -18.96 TWh import — the keeper's headline 2025 sign-flip miss, named in miso16's own model_miss_notes as 'Next lever: MISO coal high-gas-year offer curve + seam export cap'). This run adds that lever: ONE consolidated config-gated mechanism (--miso-seam-export-limit, default OFF so miso16 and every other ISO reproduce byte-identical; verified by a 2025 control re-solve that reproduces miso16's +23.41 TWh energy-balance drift and +17.97 TWh export exactly) that is the SYMMETRIC MIRROR of the already-accepted import cap. measured_seam_import_envelope(direction='export') returns each seam's per-(month x hour-of-day) p90 of the MEASURED EIA-930 BA-to-BA net-EXPORT (+sum(mw) over the seam's DIBAs, the exact opposite sign of the import envelope), clipped at 0; inject_miso_seam_flow_limit(direction='export') raises each seam's export-sink hour-varying lower bound (FleetArrays.min_gen, the same export-sink mechanism CAISO's inject_interchange_shape uses) to that envelope. A net-import seam (PJM: measured export ~0.00 GW) clips export to ~0 so cheap coal can no longer flood east; a net-export seam (South/TVA: measured export ~2.0 GW) keeps its measured export headroom. RESULT (full 3-year re-solve vs the miso16 keeper): TOTAL net-interchange |error| 52.0 -> 23.5 TWh and TOTAL |energy-balance drift| 36.8 -> 20.5 TWh, both roughly halved with NO error-shuffling (both improve). Per year -- 2025: net interchange model +17.97 (export) -> -4.29 (import), SIGN FIXED (actual -18.96); energy-balance drift +23.41 (out of tol) -> +1.17 TWh (INSIDE +/-3.0); coal 231.6 -> 222.1 (toward EIA-923 201.0); gas 222.9 -> 210.2 (toward EIA-923 207.6); interchange duration-curve RMSE 4372 -> 2037 MW. 2024: net import 8.3 -> 15.0 TWh (toward actual 23.1, +6.7 closer). 2023: net import 37.6 -> 38.7 (actual 37.9; ~neutral, the cap barely binds -- 2023 is import-dominated). No magic number and no curve fit: the cap is a measured transfer-capability ceiling from the directed-flow duration curve, forward-reproducible and flow-responsive, the same admissibility class as the accepted import cap (claude.md #1/#11/#12). No unit pinned to its CEMS output; no input rescaled so the model output lands on actuals; the p90 percentile is shared with the import cap, NOT tuned to the net-MWh residual. Determination NOT-YET (the broader MISO gas/import under-run persists -- see model_miss_notes), but strictly more structurally faithful than miso16 on net interchange AND energy balance across all three years.

model_miss_notes: Exceptions ledger EMPTY by design: every remaining out-of-tolerance criterion is a genuine MODEL MISS for a later lever, not an accepted measured-input limitation. (1) 2023/2024 NEGATIVE energy-balance drift (-13.52 / -5.78 TWh, both exceed +/-3.0) is the now-EXPOSED gas+import UNDER-RUN, NOT caused by the export cap: 2024 gas 233.7 vs EIA-923 257.8 (-24 TWh) and 2023 gas 220.6 vs 249.0 (-28 TWh) remain under, and capping the spurious South-seam export removed the surplus generation that had been masking the under-run as a balanced sheet (2023 drift was already ~-12.4 in miso16; the cap moved it only -1.1 via +1.1 TWh more import). The model now imports more toward actual (2024 8.3->15.0 of an actual 23.1) but its domestic CC fleet under-generates -- the correct, more-faithful exposure of the pre-existing miss per claude.md #11, to be fixed at root (MISO CC offer curve / seam import deliverability lift) rather than re-buried by relaxing the cap. (2) 2025 still UNDER-imports (model -4.29 vs actual -18.96 TWh): the export sign and energy balance are fixed, but the import-side under-model (PJM neighbor-price over-anchoring / eastern seam deliverability) leaves ~14 TWh of import unrealised -- the SAME import-side lever as (1), orthogonal to the export cap. (3) The export-cap percentile is held at p90, identical to the import cap, deliberately NOT tuned per-year to shrink the 2024 over-correction -- doing so would fit the residual; the residual is a real gas under-run, not a cap-calibration knob. Next lever for the keeper line: MISO CC_REGULAR offer curve + high-gas-year coal offer + a measured eastern-PJM import deliverability lift, addressing the gas/import under-run that this run exposes.
